fair_value_reason: Round-2 inputs are now consistent across agents: NTM EPS ~$9.9-10.05, NTM revenue ~$4.1-4.15B, ~$2.6B net cash, ~85M fully diluted shares. At the mean multiples (~38.8x P/E, ~7.7x EV/sales), P/E gives ~$388 and EV/sales ~$402. Weighting the P/E leg more heavily because SBC is ~21% of revenue, and allowing for March-guide risk, gives ~$388, the round-2 agent mean ($388.6), down from my round-1 $390.

thesis_triggers.event: About $240 (-33%): ~5.4x today's NTM EV/sales (~$3.3B) or ~4.4x Sep-2027 NTM revenue (~$4.1B), inside the Mar-Apr 2026 low zone ($216-260) and near where the last two March prints landed. Reaching it without a broad market crash would most likely mean a FY28 guide well below ~18% in March 2027 (confirming the guide-implied +14-16% Q4), Atlas sliding toward 20%, or go-to-market departures during the CEO search. Agents range $230-245; the correction is to the multiple description, not the level.

supervisor_summary: Round 2 converged: every agent adopted the round-1 corrections, the fair-value range narrowed to $366-405 (mean $389), and the cross-agent ladder spread fell by a third while the mean barely moved (P(close >= $356 on 2027-09-30) = 0.523). My checks confirmed the new points the agents raised: Q2's beat was partly lumpy EA revenue, the last two March guides caused one-day drops of 27% and 22%, and npm data show relative share loss to Postgres. What is left is judgment on multiples, so I keep the round-2 mean ladder with low confidence, a ~$388 fair value and a $240 thesis break. The March 2027 FY28 guide, not the CEO search, is the event that decides whether the stock re-rates.
key_drivers: The March 2027 FY28 guide: the FY27 guide implies Q4 +14-16% against a +27% comparison, and the last two March prints fell 27% and 22% in a day.
Beat quality: Q2 beat its guide by 5.1%, but EA & other swung from +13% (Q1) to +36% (Q2); the H2 raise was mainly Atlas, which has held ~29% for five quarters.
Earnings power: NTM non-GAAP EPS at Sep-2027 ~$9.9-10.05 and NTM revenue ~$4.1B on 20% growth and +150bp/yr margins; SBC at ~21% of revenue caps the multiple.
Leadership: interim CEO Ittycheria (part-time risk as a Sequoia partner); naming a permanent CEO is the main re-rating catalyst.
Relative mindshare loss to Postgres (npm 'pg' downloads +345% y/y vs 'mongodb' +64%) is a multiple cap and bear-tail driver; it is not yet visible in Atlas growth.
